articles.headline: Suljovic apologises but faces probe over inciting jeers and alleged sexist comments
keyFacts: Mensur Suljovic has been referred to the Darts Regulation Authority for inciting crowd jeers against Ross Smith and making alleged sexist comments.
The incident occurred during the Swiss Darts Trophy when Suljovic encouraged the crowd to boo Smith during a match decider.
Suljovic subsequently issued an apology, stating that emotions got the better of him and that his remarks were inappropriate.
body: Mensur Suljovic referred to darts regulator for inciting jeers against Ross Smith and alleged sexist comments as Austrian issues apology

Mensur Suljovic has been referred to the Darts Regulation Authority for his incitement of jeers against Ross Smith in their clash at the Swiss Darts Trophy; he has also been referred over his alleged sexist comments in an interview about the incident; the Austrian has issued an apology
Monday 12 October 2026 18:23, UK

Mensur Suljovic's crowd incitement during his match against Ross Smith and his alleged sexist comments in his on-stage interview regarding the incident have been referred to the Darts Regulation Authority.
The Austrian encouraged the crowd to boo the Englishman during a last-leg decider in their third-round clash at the Swiss Darts Trophy on Sunday afternoon.
He was later asked about the incident in an on-stage interview and used an allegedly sexist comment to describe how Smith reacted.

Suljovic said: "Ross Smith is one of the best players in the world - what's the bloke complaining about? He's got to play his game; otherwise, he's welcome to go home.
"Women, women - they're always complaining, sorry. Sorry, you don't do that. I fully accept him as one of the very best darts players.
"OK, I've been riling up the crowd a bit, just like in Germany - I need your support. I need you; without you, I can't achieve anything. Thank you, thank you very much!
"What's he complaining about? When I'm in England, everyone's against me; everywhere I go.
"And now, all of a sudden, he's complaining? He might as well just stay at home."
Suljovic apologises over incident
On Monday afternoon, Suljovic subsequently issued an apology.
"I would like to comment once again on my match against Ross Smith and the interview that followed," he said.
"The emotions got the better of me in that moment. I wanted to get the crowd behind me and, in doing so, I didn't properly realise that Ross was throwing for the match.
"Looking back, I understand that the timing was unfortunate and was perceived as unfair. I would like to apologise to Ross for that.
"Ross is, in my opinion, one of the best darts players in the world, and I have great respect for him and his achievements.
"My comment about women during the interview was also completely inappropriate. I should never have said something like that. I would like to sincerely apologise to all women for those remarks.
"Darts thrives on emotion, but fairness and respect are just as important. Yesterday, I let my emotions get the better of me.
"I'm sorry for that."
In a statement, the PDC confirmed "the matter on stage and interview has now been referred to the Darts Regulation Authority" and issued "no further comment".
The incident between Suljovic and Smith explained

Suljovic and Smith were locked at 5-5 in their best-of-11-legs clash on Sunday afternoon, with Smith having two match darts at double 18 when Suljovic gestured to the crowd to increase the volume of boos, prompting the Englishman to miss the target and hand his opponent a chance to steal the match.
Suljovic then nailed double 10 with his final dart to complete the checkout and seal victory.
His antics had left Smith frustrated, with the Englishman later taking to X to share his thoughts following the defeat.
"I don't blame Mensur for me losing that game," Smith wrote. "I missed two match darts. Simple as that.
"Obviously, it's impossible for me to know what he's doing behind my back when I'm throwing apart from the crowd's response.
"Karma will come around."
Suljovic is no stranger to controversial incidents. The Austrian denied intentionally provoking Joe Cullen during a World Championship clash last December.

Cullen branded his opponent's pace of play as "cheating" and "not darts" after becoming frustrated by the length of time he was taking to retrieve his darts and celebrate, with referee Kirk Bevans even forced to intervene.
Webster: There is a time and place for it and it was 'poor form'
Sky Sports Darts' Mark Webster on the incident between Smith and Suljovic (speaking before the apology)...
"Obviously with regards to the weekend, it was poor form for Mensur Suljovic.
"I think every player can use the crowd to their advantage, but there's a time to do it, isn't there?
"It's not while the player's throwing, particularly not on match darts.
"Fair play to Ross, he came out and said he didn't even see it and it didn't put him off, he still should have won the game.
"Mensur kind of doubled down on it as well. Like I said, get the crowd involved, players do it, it's part of the game now, but not on match darts and geeing them up when he's on match darts.
"He has used tactics in the past, hasn't he, in terms of slowing players down.
"That's fine, it's not against the rules, but sort of egging on the crowd when Ross on match darts wasn't good.
"I'm sure the DRA will get involved now, it's not good sportsmanship, is it? Rightly so, he should get fined.
"As long as he recognises that he's done wrong, he hasn't at the minute, but when he recognises that he's done wrong, it's the timing of it, isn't it, that's the poorest.
"I'm sure he'll realise and a fine will come his way. He should learn from it and he should never do it again, not on match darts."

articles.headline: He-Man Sets Official Return in 2027 With 'Dragon Pearl of Destruction'
keyFacts: Clear River Games announced that the action game He-Man and the Masters of the Universe: Dragon Pearl of Destruction will launch on Feb. 4, 2027.
Bitmap Bureau is developing the retro-style beat 'em up game, which features four playable characters and 13 levels.
The game will receive a physical release on Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X, alongside digital availability on multiple platforms.
body: Just in time for He-Man’s birthday, Clear River Games revealed the release date for He-Man and the Masters of the Universe: Dragon Pearl of Destruction, an upcoming action game based on this long-running series. Thankfully, the wait for Prince Adam and his buddies won't be long.

Clear River Games also confirmed that Dragon Pearl of Destruction will have a physical release for Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X. It will also be available digitally on those platforms, as well as PS4, Windows PC, and Xbox One. The game will be released on Feb. 4, 2027.
What kind of game is He-Man and the Masters of the Universe: Dragon Pearl of Destruction?

He-Man and the Masters of the Universe: Dragon Pearl of Destruction is a retro-style beat ‘em up. The game is being developed by Bitmap Bureau, a studio that’s quite familiar with arcade-era-inspired tie-ins to classic franchises. In 2025, the team released the 2D run-and-gun Terminator 2D: No Fate, which received solid reviews despite criticisms for its short length. Before that, the team worked on the beat ‘em up Final Vendetta and the hack-and-slash Battle Axe.

Dragon Pearl of Destruction has four playable characters — He-Man, Teela, Man-at-Arms, and She-Ra — each with different movesets and magic abilities. The Steam page indicates it will have 13 levels, suggesting a relatively short playtime, as is fairly common in this genre.
Is He-Man having a revival?

Beyond the upcoming game, He-Man recently hit the screen in this summer’s Masters of the Universe live-action movie. While the film performed relatively well with critics, it flopped at the box office, grossing $114 million on a $170 to 200 million budget, although it was Prime Video’s most-streamed movie for several weeks in a row.

Beyond this, there have been plenty of recent He-Man TV shows. The animated series Masters of the Universe ran on Netflix from July 2021 to January 2024 for 15 episodes total. Before that, She-Ra: Princesses of Power ran from 2018 to 2020 for 52 episodes, a reboot of the ‘80s series (which was a spin-off of He-Man and the Masters of the Universe). That series received critical acclaim and attracted a large fandom thanks to its interesting characters, strong writing, and central queer relationship between She-Ra and Catra.

articles.headline: Business-hating Democrats poised to haul execs before Congress if they win control of House
keyFacts: The potential targets range from tech giants and Wall Street firms to airlines, healthcare companies and corporate landlords, as Democrats prepare to scrutinize businesses over their ties to President Trump and practices affecting the cost of living, Bloomberg reported Monday.
Top House Dem Hakeem Jeffries, who’s poised to become speaker if Democrats win control of the chamber, has already been pounding the drum.

body: The potential targets range from tech giants and Wall Street firms to airlines, healthcare companies and corporate landlords, as Democrats prepare to scrutinize businesses over their ties to President Trump and practices affecting the cost of living, Bloomberg reported Monday.
Top House Dem Hakeem Jeffries, who’s poised to become speaker if Democrats win control of the chamber, has already been pounding the drum.
“There’s a cost to the American people of the out-of-control corruption that has been visited upon them by Donald Trump and MAGA extremists,” the Brooklyn lefty said over the summer.

Amazon, Apple, Comcast, Meta, Microsoft and Nvidia have already received letters from Democratic lawmakers demanding information about their donations to Trump’s White House ballroom project, Bloomberg reported.

Democrats are expected to examine whether companies that financially supported Trump’s projects obtained preferential treatment from the administration, as well as deals involving tariff exemptions, drug prices and government equity stakes.
Walmart, Target, Nike and Energizer Holdings have been pressed about tariff refunds, as have Amazon, Apple and Motorola.
Other inquiries have focused on surveillance pricing at airlines including Delta, United and American.

“There is no fare product Delta has ever used, is testing or plans to use that targets customers with individualized offers based on personal information or otherwise,” a Delta spokesperson told The Post.

“A variety of market forces drive the dynamic pricing model that’s been used in the global industry for decades, with new tech simply streamlining this process,” the flack added. “Delta always complies with regulations around pricing and disclosures.”
Democrats’ inquiries have also extended to data center investments involving Blackstone, KKR, BlackRock and Brookfield Infrastructure Partners, as well as rent costs at corporate-owned properties.
“This is part of our practice, and we have clients that we are advising on,” he told The Post.
The consequences for companies that are called to testify before Congress could extend well beyond embarrassing headlines, Scharf warned.
“We’ve seen oversight and congressional investigations turn into referrals and criminal referrals. We’ve seen them turn into class action lawsuits,” he said.
“It’s more than public relations. Certainly, on the public relations side of things, you only need to look bad for 10 seconds on TikTok,” Scharf added.

Dems are widely expected to take the House, with the Cook Political Report predicting a net gain five-to-15 seats. The razor-thin margin in the Senate will come down to a handful of contests, observers say.

Some of the nation’s biggest companies aren’t waiting until Election Day to prepare for a possible Democratic takeover, hiring politically connected advisers and weighing how to respond to congressional investigations.

Skydance, the media goliath born out of the merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, has hired former Democratic aides to bolster their Washington representation — as has prediction market operator Kalshi.

Private companies could prove particularly vulnerable because they lack some of the legal privileges available to White House officials seeking to resist congressional investigations, Bloomberg noted.
Businesses also risk alienating customers and shareholders if they refuse to cooperate, the article said.
Spokespersons for KKR, Microsoft, Meta and Amazon declined comment when reached by The Post.
The Post has sought comment from Jeffries and the White House.

articles.headline: Hackers heat up refrigerators at hundreds of supermarkets: "Unprecedented"
keyFacts: Major French supermarket chains confirmed a cyberattack forced hundreds of stores to raise refrigerator temperatures, destroying fresh and frozen food.
Paris prosecutors confirmed an investigation has been opened into the large-scale attack, which also reportedly sparked fires.
Manufacturer Danfoss stated that most of the affected equipment consisted of legacy products that no longer receive software or security updates.
body: Major French supermarket chains on Monday said they were hit by a cyberattack that caused their refrigerators to shoot up in temperature in hundreds of stores, forcing spoiled food to be thrown away and raising concerns about food security.
Top retailers E. Leclerc, Intermarché and Cooperative U confirmed to AFP they suffered a cyberattack that Cooperative U's chief executive described as "unprecedented."

"Food security requires more attention at all levels," said the EU's food and agriculture commissioner Christophe Hansen on X, condemning the attack and saying such "exploitation of food" was now a "reality."
At least 300 shops of Intermarché or its Netto brand were targeted, along with over 100 Cooperative U outlets, and several E. Leclerc stores, the retailers told AFP in separate statements.

"Targeting equipment essential to the preservation of fresh products and to the food supply of the French people is of extreme gravity and is unprecedented," Cooperative U CEO Dominique Schelcher wrote on X.
Paris prosecutors confirmed the attack, which reportedly also hit other major chains, and also indicated it had sparked fires.
BFM TV said hackers "managed to remotely trigger the forced defrosting of the refrigeration systems in numerous stores."
The affected branches will have to "throw away all of the products" that are fresh and frozen, Intermarché told AFP.
Carrefour said 80 of its supermarkets were attacked but that the vast majority of its 6,000 stores were not affected, according to the Reuters news agency.
E. Leclerc confirmed to AFP "that a cyberattack affected one of its refrigeration equipment suppliers," resulting in "repercussions on the operation of refrigeration systems in several stores."
A source close to the issue said refrigeration control systems from Danish manufacturer Danfoss were targeted.
Danfoss told AFP in a statement that most of the affected equipment was "legacy" products which "no longer receive software or security updates."

It said its AK-SM800 and AK-SC355 fridge regulator systems were notably affected, with a version of the former using "outdated firmware." It added that it had long advised supermarkets to update from those models. Danfoss gave no figures on how many systems were affected.

Dutch supermarket operator Ahold Delhaize, which also has operations in the United States, said it was also dealing with a "security issue" in its network, Reuters reported. A phone app for the retailer told clients that due to a "cybersecurity incident" it was unable to deliver groceries.
"Large-scale cyberattack"

A person close to French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said France's cybersecurity agency had already identified "a vulnerability in software supplied by a Danish company and has contacted the vendor."

"It is liaising with its European counterparts, as other countries may be affected," and is seeking "to identify other French companies involved in order to alert them" and "prevent the spread," the source added.

The office of the Paris prosecutor confirmed to AFP that an investigation has been opened into "the large-scale cyberattack affecting the refrigerators of several major food retail chains across France."
The probe will help "identify the victims and establish the link with the damage they reported in terms of foodstuff losses and the outbreak of fires," the prosecutor's office said.
Intermarché condemned the food waste and financial losses resulting from the attack, without providing figures.
BFM TV said temperatures were "altered remotely, resulting in the destruction of stocks of fresh and frozen products."
Rising fears of hybrid attacks
The incident comes against the background of growing concern over the potential havoc that can be caused in Europe in all sectors by malicious actors carrying out cyberattacks.

President Emmanuel Macron, a strong supporter of Ukraine in its fight against the Russian invasion, last month ordered measures to protect France's critical infrastructure from Russian "hybrid attacks."

Industrial equipment such as refrigeration units, long isolated from the internet, is now connected via sensors or remote monitoring systems, Antoine Hautin of cybersecurity consultancy Almond told AFP.
By likely affecting hundreds of units simultaneously, the attack demonstrated "a certain level of sophistication," he added.

articles.headline: Why Kentucky's upset win over LSU cost school half a million dollars
keyFacts: Kentucky defeated LSU 35-34 in overtime during a Week 6 college football game.
Kentucky fans rushed the field after the victory, violating Southeastern Conference rules regarding competition areas.
SEC policy requires Kentucky to pay a 500,000 dollar fine directly to LSU.
body: LSU exits Week 6 of the 2026 college football season with its playoff hopes barely hanging on, falling to 4-2 with a loss to Kentucky. The Tigers will, however, head into Week 7 with some extra cash.

The Wildcats stunned Lane Kiffin's squad in front of their home fans on Saturday with a 35-34 win in overtime, marking LSU's second loss of the season and a huge victory for Will Stein. But because Kentucky fans stormed the field, the school will have to pay up.
Under SEC rules, Kentucky will be forced to send hundreds of thousands of dollars to LSU.
Here's what to know about the SEC rules that will result in Kentucky paying LSU for its field storm.
MORE: First look at college football's loaded Week 7 slate
Why Kentucky's upset win over LSU cost school half a million dollars

Immediately after quarterback Kenneth Minchey's game-winning two-point conversion in overtime against LSU, Kentucky fans rushed from the stands and onto the field on Saturday, celebrating the upset 35-34 win against the country's No. 10-ranked team.
In the moment, it was joyous for Kentucky and its fanbase. But in hindsight, it was a pricey decision made by the fans.

— Barstool Sports (@barstoolsports) October 11, 2026

SEC policies since 2023 have called for a fine to be paid to the opposing school if a team's fans storm the field, per Front Office Sports. And since 2025, every field-storming violation has equated with a $500,000 fine. That means Kentucky will now owe LSU $500,000 for the field storming.

The rule of paying the fine to the opposing school only sticks for SEC play — if an SEC team is fined for field-storming against a non-conference opponent, the fine would then be paid to the SEC’s post-graduate scholarship fund.

Kentucky becomes the first SEC school to deal with the field-storming fine this season. Since 2025, when the SEC changed the fine from $100,000 to $500,000 for a first-time offense, only one SEC school has been fined for the violation. Mississippi State fans stormed the field last season after beating Arizona State.

According to Front Office Sports, SEC policy stats that “institutions shall limit access to competition areas to participating student-athletes, coaches, officials, support personnel and properly credentialed or authorized individuals at all times. For the safety of participants and spectators alike, at no time before, during or after a contest may spectators enter the competition area." However, with conference permission, fans can "celebrate on the playing surface once all visiting team personnel and game officials have safely exited the field or court."

The SEC first began imposing fines for rushing the field in 2004, per The Athletic, and the conference is able to waive the fine if it finds that "opposing personnel and officials were able to reach their locker room before fans flooded the field."
Kentucky's field-storming won't just cost the Wildcats — it will put some more cash in LSU's pocket.

articles.headline: 2027 Rivian R2 review: The Goldilocks electric SUV
keyFacts: Rivian's third electric vehicle, the mid-size R2 SUV, hit roads earlier this year with a starting price under $60,000.
The R2 features a spacious cabin, 5.2 cubic feet of front trunk storage, and a homegrown infotainment system powered by Google mapping.
The R2 Performance model delivers 656 horsepower, reaching 0 to 60 mph in 3.6 seconds with a lighter curb weight than the larger R1S.
body: 2027 Rivian R2 review: The Goldilocks electric SUV
It’s not too big, it’s not too small and it’s not too expensive. It’s just right.

Rivian's first vehicle — the R1T — initially hit the roads in 2021. Despite the industry's best efforts, electric trucks just haven't enjoyed the same popularity as their gas-powered counterparts. Rivian followed that up with the R1S in 2022, which added more room for passengers while also serving as the primary platform for future development. But with three rows of seats and a starting price of over $80,000, it's a bit too big and too expensive to have true mainstream appeal.

Earlier this year, Rivian's third EV — the R2 — hit the roads. The company distilled nearly all of its best features and tech into a family-friendly mid-size SUV. It blends the ruggedness of an off-roader with the civility of a buttoned-up grocery runner for under $60,000 (or much less depending on the spec). It's not too big, it's not too expensive and it has the right blend of tech and style, which sort of makes the Rivian R2 the closest thing to a Goldilocks EV SUV on sale today.
Design

In many respects, the R2 looks like Rivian took the R1S's design, put it in a photocopier and then spit out a new vehicle at 75 percent size. But that's not quite right because Rivian chief design officer Jeff Hammoud previously said the R1 is actually based on an early concept for the R2. The company liked it so much it ended up becoming the template for both models. Naturally, this means the R2 has a lot of the same design cues as its bigger sibling, including a boxy body with flush door handles, chunky bumpers and the company's signature pill-shaped headlights. It's a good look that balances the desire to have the brawny exterior you expect from a rugged SUV without straying too far into retro-inspired designs like you get from many of its gas-powered rivals — such as the current Bronco and Wrangler.

Rivian has also done a great job on integrating a lot of off-road features into the R2 chassis, like the built-in tow hooks in front and recessed mounts for a roof rack on top. The Performance Launch Model I tested also had Rivian's optional tow package, which includes a standard 7-pin connector and a concealed hitch. In the cargo area, there's both a 12v accessory socket and 120v outlet to power pretty much any gadget you would need. If that's still not enough, the R2 even supports bi-directional charging (both V2L and V2H), though we're still waiting on Rivan to release the accompanying charging adapter.

Unlike some other EV SUVs that have ditched their frunks, the R2 still has a good-sized cargo area under its hood that offers 5.2 cubic feet of storage. Plus, there's a drain in case you want to use it as a cooler for tailgating or storing wet gear. All together, you get a very capable car for all sorts of trips and conditions, but without the vehicle feeling like it needs to scream about its versatility.

Some of the R2's best features are things like its Matrix LED headlights, which adjust automatically to driving conditions and oncoming vehicles. It feels like there's a little robot manning each beam to shine it exactly where you need it. And while the R2 doesn't have a split tailgate like you get on the R1S, Rivian still included a rear hatch with a retractable window, so you can lower it to transport longer items or just catch some fresh air. There's even a button that lets you lower all four windows and the rear windshield with a single touch, which is a really nice features when the weather is just right.

I also appreciate a lot of the little details hidden throughout the vehicle, like the button for the rear hatch. Instead of being located dead center, it sits off to the left just a touch, directly above the "V" in Rivian around back. So even though there isn't an explicit call out to where it is, you always know where to press. Annoyingly, there are some small oversights, like when I discovered that in order to remove the rear seat headrests, you need a little pin tool. This became a minor issue when I was trying to install car seats for my kids. While there are handy LATCH (Lower Anchors and Tethers for Children) points, there wasn't an easy way of threading a strap through the headset to reach the loop on the back of the rear bench without that tool.

My one personal gripe is that because the R1S and R2 look so similar, I wish Rivian had given it its own unique design trait — like the slanted C-pillar on the R3. Rivian's upcoming compact SUV won't arrive until sometime in 2028, but because the company has already revealed its design, I've lost count of the number of people who have gushed to me about how good it looks. It's a bit sad that the R2 doesn't have its own signature style.
Interior

On the inside, the R2 features a cabin that blends modern minimalism with just enough warm accents, which makes things feel spacious and airy but still cozy at the same time. One thing that immediately struck me in comparison to my Mach-E is that even though both cars are essentially the same length (185 inches), the R2 felt noticeably roomier. The dash is made from upcycled birch in either a charcoal or light gray finish, while the infotainment has just enough physical controls to balance out its big 15.6-inch main display and 11.5-inch driver's display. There are also two glove boxes, and you don't need to search for any kind of touch controls to open them. You just press in and voila.

Meanwhile, there are Rivian's Haptic Halo Wheels, which feel like someone took two scroll wheels out of some high-end mice and embedded them into the R2's steering wheel. You can spin them up and down to do things like adjust volume or change your speed when using assisted driving modes, but you can also push them left and right to change tracks and whatnot. It's really simple and really intuitive. And behind the wheel, you get traditional stalks for controlling things like the gear selector, blinkers and windshield wipers.

Seats are big and somewhat comfy, though for my taste, I wish they had a touch more lumbar support. On premium and performance models, you also get heated and ventilated seats, the latter of which I enjoyed a lot thanks to our unseasonably warm fall weather in the northeast.

There are also numerous USB-C ports scattered through the vehicle, including one in the back of both front seat headrests. There's a built-in wireless charger in the center console, too. Strangely though, you only get one of those for the driver's side, which could be annoying on a longer trip when multiple people need to top up their phones.

Meanwhile, the second row seats are quite spacious, even for a six-foot tall adult like me. There's ample leg and head room, and from the back, you can more easily appreciate the R2's panoramic glass roof. The rear seats fold down in a 60-40 split so you can maximize passenger room even when you're transporting things like skis and snowboards, while the cargo area offers around 30 cubic feet of storage even with the rear seats up. And if you lift the floor, there's even more room to stash gear.

Making use of every little nook and cranny seems to be something Rivian is quite good at. In addition to all the little cubbies and hidden drink holders stashed throughout the car, the Premium and Performance versions of the R2 even come with little touches like an included flashlight that can be neatly stashed inside the driver's door.
Tech and infotainment

Unlike so many cars that rely on support from Android Auto and Apple CarPlay to make their infotainment functional, Rivian has taken a homegrown approach. It shows that when a system is designed well, you don't need help from your phone's OS. All of the car's core functions are divided neatly into different tabs for things like music, drive modes, navigation and charging. Mapping is powered by Google, so you get a wealth of info, though there are little oddities that still stick out. For example, Rivian's voice assistant pronounces Houston street in NYC the same as the city in Texas, which for locals is a clear sign that you don't live here. But that's largely superficial, because you still get things like traffic alerts and police sightings directly on the map.

The charging screen makes it easy to get quick updates on things like range, energy use and nearby chargers while the video tab makes it easy to access the R2's cameras. Those are used for parking or checking out the feed from Rivian's Gear Guard system, which acts as a built-in dash cam to record footage while driving or stationary. I will die on this hill, but I really think every modern car should have the ability to use a car's onboard cameras to save clips in case of an accident. I'm really glad Rivian's didn't skimp on this functionality like a lot of other car makers.

Selecting tunes is as simple as signing into your Apple Music, SiriusXM or Spotify account. Unfortunately, my service of choice, YouTube Music, isn't supported. However, the bigger caveat is that you'll also need a subscription to Rivian's Connect+ service, which runs $15 a month or $150 a year, that includes other handy features like an in-car Wi-Fi hotspot, video streaming and more.

The one wrinkle is that Connect+ is also meant to include the Rivian Assistant, which adds support for enhanced voice controls and texting integration from your phone. It's currently available on both the R1T and R1S, but it hasn't been ported over to the R2 just yet. Thankfully, Rivian is planning to add it sometime before the end of the year (potentially as soon as this month). I'm not a fan of buying promises though, so if you haven't paid for a reservation, this is one of the features I would wait for before putting my money down on an R2.

In the time since I reviewed the R1S, Rivian added the option to replace the typical chirp you get when locking the car with an owl's hoot, which my two-year-old loved so much she threw a tantrum the one time I switched it back.

Then there's the Rivian app, which makes it easy to keep tabs on the car, lock/unlock the doors, activate climate control remotely and more. On my Galaxy Z Fold 8, keyless entry worked with the Samsung Wallet app for easy integration. Once I set it up, it was flawless during my week-long test session. Managing the important features from my phone was simple, straightforward and reliable, and I think a lot of competing car makers could learn a lot from Rivian's software.
Driving

If you simply look at the numbers, you might think that an R2 Performance lags way behind a top-spec R1S, which offers up to 1,025 horsepower with its quad-motor option. But that's not a fair comparison because a dual-motor R1S (533 hp and 0 to 60 in 4.5 seconds) actually has less horsepower and oomph than an R2 Performance (656 hp and a 0 to 60 time of 3.6 seconds). And when you combine that with a lighter curb weight of around 5,000 pounds (versus 6,600 to 7,100 pounds for the R1S), you get an SUV that pulls like a herd of stampeding buffalo. Torque is instantaneous, which makes accelerating onto an on-ramp or passing aggressively delightful. The R2 has so much power that even in its stiffest ride setting, you can still feel the entire car lurch upwards when you slam down on the accelerator.

Now there's no getting around that the R2's suspension is on the firmer side of things, even when it's on Rivian's more forgiving moderate setting. But I don't mind that, as that's sort of expected from a tallish SUV, plus it still lets you feel the road while providing good driver feedback regarding grip and stability. The R2 offers multiple levels of regen which makes one-pedal driving a breeze. Furthermore, while I didn't take it on the trails, the R2's off-road DNA showed through when I drove it across gravel and cobblestones. It casually eliminated the kind of excess turbulence that can result in a truly teeth-chattering ride.

I also appreciate how Rivian didn't mess with the drive mode tab in the infotainment, which serves as a central menu for adjusting things like ride feel, regen, stability and more. This tab also lets you easily see stats like motor temperature, tire pressure and even things like the orientation of your wheels and the elevation. Those last two items can be very helpful in rough terrain.

For those who opt for Autonomy+ (which costs $50 a month or $2,500 for a one-time purchase, after your initial 60-day free trial on new vehicles), you'll get access to Universal Hands-free driving across more than 3.5 million miles of roads in the US and Canada. On the highway, hands-free driving was sublime. It easily handled lane changes and congested roads without drama. In some ways, it even felt a touch smoother than BlueCruise on my Mach-E, as the R2 followed curves a bit more gracefully compared to Ford's system, which can feel a bit robotic at times. I also really like how Rivian allows you to make micro steering adjustments when needed, which on other vehicles will often kick you out of hands-free mode.

That said, while you can use hands-free driving on some surface streets (you'll know when the little icon lights up on the driver's digital cluster display), Rivian's tech needs a little more polishing there. I found that sometimes it would let me activate hands-free mode for just a few seconds, before quickly disabling it when it noticed road markers weren't distinct enough. This is also highly dependent on the specific road and how nearby lines look. So while you can go hands-free on some local streets, the R2 needs a little extra baby sitting. That's okay, because we know it's not meant to be 100 percent autonomous yet, right? Right. You can take your hands off the wheel, but don't close your eyes.

Finally, there are some other little touches that I really like, such as the camera feed from the sideview mirrors that automatically pops up in the driver's instruments when you hit your blinkers. This tech is becoming more popular on new cars and I hope it becomes standard equipment soon. Same goes for the bird's eye 360-view that activates when the car senses that you're maneuvering in tight spaces or when you shift into reverse.
Range and charging

Both the premium and performance version of the R2 promise 330 miles of range from an 88kWh battery. Based on my experience, that seems about spot on. That is, assuming you can resist the urge not to take advantage of the R2's power. During a drive of around 100 miles (one third city driving and two-thirds highway), I found the EV averaged around 3.25 miles per kWh. Efficiency wasn't quite as good on surface streets where there's a lot of stop and go, or when you go above 70 mph, but if you're looking to maximize range, getting above 300 miles per charge is very doable.

As for charging, the R2 comes standard with an NACS and you can easily get a CCS adapter if you need it. That said, while I certainly wouldn't say it's slow, I feel like the R2's charging speed is somewhat mediocre. Rivan says that the car's 400-volt architecture supports recharging at up to 230 kW, but when I tested this out at an 350kW EVGO station, the R2's charging curve topped out at 161kW. That allowed it to deliver on Rivian's claim of being able to go from a 10 percent state of charge to 80 percent in around 27 minutes. This is fine, but it's still a touch slower than rivals like the Hyundai Ioniq 5.
Trims and pricing

The R2 Performance with Launch Package (which is what I drove for this review) is on sale today and starts at $57,990. It features a dual-motor AWD drivetrain with 656 hp, 330 miles of range and a 0 to 60 time of 3.6 seconds. This trim also comes with Rivian's Autonomy+ tech, 21-inch wheels with all-season tires, Matrix headlights, a compact spare and an included key fob.

The R2's premium spec starts at $53,990 for a dual-motor AWD system with 450 hp, 330 miles of range and a 0 to 60 time of 4.6 seconds. This trim still comes with Matrix headlights, standard tow hooks, premium audio and 20-inch wheels, but things like Autonomy+ and the tow packages are now optional extras. This spec is slated to go on sale sometime in late 2026.

Finally, the standard R2 starts at $44,900 for a single-motor RWD setup with 350 hp, 275 miles of range and a 0 to 60 time of 5.9 seconds. Optional upgrades include a larger battery pack for longer range or a dual-motor AWD config alongside things like Autonomy+. However, this trim won't be available until sometime in the spring of 2027.
Wrap-up

Driving the R2 is a somewhat strange experience after reviewing the R1S last year. In fact, Rivian's two EV SUVs look so similar that when my neighbors saw the R2 parked on the street, they thought I was actually testing its bigger sibling. I's a similar situation on the inside, where the R2 so closely mirrors Rivian's three-row model (with one less bench, of course) that sometimes you forget that you're driving around in a significantly smaller vehicle that costs between $20,000 to $30,000 less (or more depending on the config). But in a way, that's a big complement to the R2. It has nearly everything I liked about the R1S, but in a more compact package.

I do have a few tiny reservations, such as waiting for the Rivian Assistant to be officially released. I also hope that hands-free driving on surface streets gets some additional tuning. The R2's charging speed could be a touch faster too. But those are very minor dings against what is otherwise an incredibly full-featured and very capable EV. With the R2, Rivian is proving that just because an electric SUV is smaller and more affordable, that doesn't mean it has to make major trade-offs to its style, power and tech compared to the rest of its siblings. And for a family of four, the R2 feels like the Goldilocks SUV that could make people who currently drive gas-powered rivals jump to an EV and never look back.

articles.headline: Trump reposts Kid Rock’s warnings of religious ‘civil war’: ‘El-Sayed’s a wolf in sheep’s clothing’

Trump previously referred to El-Sayed on social media as a jihadist lunatic who wants to see the United States fail.
body: Trump shared the clip late Sunday of the 55-year-old Christian singer warning Lara Trump on her Fox News show of his fears specifically for Dearborn, the Detroit suburb where he and multiple generations of his family were born and raised.
Rock said that while he knows “there are extremists and there are milder versions of it … I don’t want my grandkids to one day have to fight some civil war over religious ideology.”

Trump shared the clip without comment. But he days earlier referred to El-Sayed as a “Jihadist lunatic who hates our Country, the Black People of Detroit, and wants to see the U.S. fail.”

articles.headline: Burnham says ‘public will be the boss’ in any future decision about closer relationship with the EU – as it happened
keyFacts: Andy Burnham told MPs the UK must seek a deeper EU partnership, insisting the British public will decide any future relationship.
Burnham stated losing access to European databases weakened UK immigration control, though EU president Ursula von der Leyen is open to restoring data sharing.
Burnham said he will work to secure an arrangement on immigration data sharing at an EU-UK summit in November.
body: Burnham says 'public will be the boss' in any future decisions about closer relationship with EU
Burnham confirmed that he wanted to open a discussion about the UK’s future relationship with the EU.
If we are serious, if we are serious about promoting growth, controlling immigration, upholding our values and security, it is a conversation we must have.
The status quo is not good enough for Britain.
Worse, it would be a major dereliction of duty to turn away.
We need to take a calm, clear-eyed, rational look at the world as it is today to consider what is best for our country.
Our immediate priority is securing a successful outcome at the summit, and I believe we should then set up a serious dialogue about the different options for our relationship in the long term.
At every stage, the British public will be the boss, and I am clear that public opinion currently supports a pragmatic approach like the one I am suggesting.

Andy Burnham has told MPs that it would be a “dereliction of duty” not to seek deeper partnership with the EU. In a long statement to MPs, he repeatedly refused to rule out taking the UK back into the EU single market after the general election. But he also insisted that the British public would be the “boss” at every stage of renegotiating the relationship. He critcised the Brexit deal negotiated by the last Tory government and said, if the opposition were genuinely committed to growth, they would accept the need to revise it. He said:
If we are serious about promoting growth, controlling immigration, upholding our values and security, it is a conversation we must have.
Burnham says von der Leyen open to giving UK better access to EU databases which would help with migration control
Lisa O’Carroll
Lisa O’Carroll is a senior Guardian correspondent covering post-Brexit issues.

Labour’s Stella Creasy asked Burnham if he accepted that it was harder for the UK to control its borders because, after Brexit, it lost access to the Eurodac database, which contains biometric data about asylum seekers. Burnham accepted this was a big problem.
He told MPs:
We are in a weaker position when it comes to controlling immigration than we were, just over 10 years ago.
It is really important as we go into this next phase that all sides of the house support the British position when we go towards this negotiation.
Is any member of this house truly saying to me this afternoon that they do not want to have access again to that European immigration information?
If they are saying that they need to be honest about it.
Later Labour’s Chris Webb asked if the forthcoming EU-UK summit would allow the UK to regain better control of immigration. Burnham replied:

One of the most positive aspects of my meeting with [EU president Ursula] von der Leyen in New York was her openness to the conversation about restoring data sharing on immigration across the EU, across Europe. That is something that Britain has long sought in the decade since Brexit. It is the control that we lost, actually, at the time of the referendum.

It’s one of the issues that doesn’t get enough attention, and it should get more, and I can say to [Webb] I will work hard to see if we can get a practical arrangement on that very issue at the summit in November.

As well as losing access to Eurodac, which would allow the UK to swiftly identify if people claiming asylum in the UK had previously applied somewhere else in the EU, with Brexit the UK also lost access to the Schengen information systems, which provide alerts on criminals and stolen goods, and the European arrest warrant database, which provides immediate alerts about fugitives.
Burnham fails to rule out eventually accepting EU freedom of movement after being challenged by Labour and Tory MPs
The Labour MP Jonathan Hinder, who represents Pendle and Clitheroe, asked Burnham to confirm that, as long as he remains PM, “there will be no return to freedom of movement”.

Burnham said that he would fully respect the Labour manifesto which ruled out joining the single market during this parliament. Being in the single market would mean the UK having to comply with freedom of movement for EU nationals.
But he went on:
What we have to look at are the options that are available for the long-term relationship. This country in the next decade needs to know where it’s going.
There are no assumptions here. And as I said in my [opening comments – see 4.01pm], the British public will be the boss of whatever, whatever is decided.

A few minutes later the Labour MP Melanie Onn, who represents Great Grimsby and Cleethorpes, said Burnham was evasive in his answer to Hinder. She asked Burnham for an assurance that, in his proposed renegotiation with the EU, the UK would not have to accept freedom of movemment, and would not have to “capitulate” and join the euro.
Burnham again sidestepped the question. He said:
As I’ve said many times this afternoon, we will honour the manifesto in full, and the red lines are in place.
Later the Conservative MP Saqib Bhatti said Burnham was evading the question. He asked Burnham for a straight yes or no: in any future renegotiation, would freedom of movement be on the table.
Burnham replied:

The honourable gentleman is getting way ahead of himself. There is no proposal for a referendum. There’s no deal on the table. All I have said is, as we go towards this negotiation, it makes sense to consider also our longer term options because it helps our European partners if they know where Britain wants to go in the future. That is all that is being said at this moment in time.
Burnham ducks question from Richard Tice about whether any of RAF Fairford suspects had Iranian diplomatic immunity

Richard Tice, the deputy leader of Reform UK, has Burnham if he could comment on “serious suggestions” that some of those arrested and bailed in relation to the RAF Fairford suspected bomb plot had Iranian diplomatic immunity.
Burnham said he would not go into detail. But he said the home secretary would make a statement about this later.
Pippa Crerar and Jessica Elgot have been talking about the Brexit/Russia row on the latest edition of the Guardian’s Politics Weekly UK podcast. You can watch it here.
Details of Burnham's meetings with Manchester City when he was city's mayor released

Andy Burnham had a formal meeting with Manchester City’s chair Khaldoon Al Mubarak at an investment summit, chatted to him in the stands at a star player’s testimonial game and was accompanied by staff from the club on official overseas visits, the Press Association reports. PA says:
Details of the prime minister’s contacts with the scandal-hit club and its Abu Dhabi owners during his time as Greater Manchester mayor were released by the combined authority.
Burnham told MPs that “all of my dealings” with Manchester City’s owners would be published.
A spokesperson for the Greater Manchester combined authority said:

In October 2021 Andy Burnham, in his role as mayor of Greater Manchester, had a formal meeting with Khaldoon Al Mubarak at the UK Government’s Global Investment Summit arranged by the Department for International Trade.

In his capacity as mayor, he was a guest of Manchester City FC at home matches on a small number of occasions, including attending Vincent Kompany’s testimonial match in September 2019, where he met the chairman informally in the stands. These have been declared in the usual way.

Also during his time as mayor, representatives of Greater Manchester sporting clubs would routinely join business delegations as part of mayoral international visits. This included representatives from Manchester United travelling to Austin and Dublin, Lancashire Cricket Club joining a delegation to India, and Manchester City FC staff supporting visits to China and Japan.
In the Commons Liam Byrne, the Labour chair of the business committee, asked Andy. Burnham to consider the case for new tariffs on Chinese imports.
He said:

The EU’s made-in-Europe proposals risks destroying any ambitions to re-industrialise our country. To avoid that peril, we are going to have to get serious with the EU in tackling unfair competition from China.

So will the prime minister reserve the right to introduce new tariffs on unfairly subsidised imports from China, so that British and European businesses have got a fair level playing field on which to compete?
Burnham replied:
I agree with him, though, that Made in Europe does present risks to British manufacturing, and I know he will have concerns about the automotive industry in the West Midlands.

I am raising those concerns with European partners. It is important that we get to an arrangement here that works for both the UK and the EU. After all, we are both trying to deal with the same issue, which is Chinese exports and the damaging effect that’s having on our industry.
So the way to approach this is to do it together, and that’s the case that we’re making to the EU.

In his response to Kemi Badenoch, Andy Burnham explicitly denied implying that the Brexit referendum result was illegitimate when he made his comment about Russian interference. (See 4.17pm.) The Conservative party has now issued a thoroughly misleading statement ignoring what he said. A spokesperson said:

The leader of the opposition just asked the prime minister, in light of his comments on Russian interference, if he thought the 2016 EU Referendum result was legitimate or illegitimate. Andy Burnham refused to answer.

There can be no doubt that his words to the Rest Is Politics were intended to cast doubt on the legitimacy of the referendum result. By not answering Kemi Badenoch’s question, Andy Burnham has all but conceded this was a deliberate ploy intended to sow more division, reopen the battles of the past, and bolster his own case for rejoining the EU.

This reads like the sort of statement which gets drafted in advance in expectation of one response in the Commons, and which then gets released anyway even though it doesn’t apply to what was actually said.
The former Tory PM Boris Johnson is also misrepresenting what Burnham said. He posted this on social media this afternoon.

This is just not true. As soon as I became foreign secretary I asked the security services the same question and they replied that there was no evidence of any successful interference in the 2016 referendum, by Russia or any other power.

Either the security services have changed their view - which would be very odd - or Burnham is lying about what he has been told. After all Starmer was in power for two years and had access to exactly the same information.
You can read what Burnham did actually say on the Rest is Politics at 10.33am.
Burnham declines invitation to condemn Trump for his 'act of treachery' in buying diesel from Putin
Ed Davey also asked Burnham to bring together a coalition of countries willing to condemn President Trump for the deal he has agreed to buy Russian diesel.
Burnham ignored this question when he replied to Davey, but the Tory MP Roger Gale challenged him on it again later. Gale asked Burnham to unequivocally condemn “this act of treachery” by Trump.
Burnham replied:
I did make it clear in my statement that, when I heard news, I was immediately on the phone to President Zelenskyy offering any help that I could provide.

And I think where Britain can best provide help is in trying to bring people back together to get a solution that works for Ukraine. And you have to think about that more than anything in these circumstances - what will be most helpful?
Ed Davey, the Lib Dem leader, praised Burnham for his comments about Brexit. He said:
His predecessor turned a blind eye to the disastrous consequences of the Conservatives’ Brexit deal, so it’s welcome to hear him recognise that damage today.
We on these benches have consistently argued that their Brexit deal has made us all poorer, weaker and less safe.
So I’m glad the prime minister has arrived at the same conclusion as we have.
But now it’s time to do something about it.
Davey said that Burnham should not revisit the Labour manifesto red lines ruling out joining a customs union or the single market this parliament.
Burnham said he thought public opinion had shifted, and people now wanted a “pragmatic” approach to Europe.
But, he went on:
I also want to maintain trust in politics. And I’m afraid I’m not prepared to revisit the red lines. in our our manifesto.
Burnham claims he's not reopening Brexit referendum - but he says he wants to be 'pragmatic'
Edward Leigh, the Conservative father of the Commons, asked if Burnham would view this as a reasonable statement. This is the statement he asked the PM to endorse.

I’ve been elected by my MPs to serve a full term of government. I’m going to get on with bread and butter issues such as the care system, pensions, asylum. And of course we would like a good, close relationship with our partners on security in Europe.
But I say this to the people – this is the prime minister speaking – I am very wary about reopening the whole Brexit wars …
And I give this absolute commitment that I would not seek to join the EU unless there was a general election first and I offer the British people a full referendum.
Burnham replied:
Can I say to the father of the house that I stand by every single one of those words.
I am not reopening the referendum. I respect the referendum result … but what I will do is take a pragmatic approach.

When I can boost growth in the British economy, when I can increase cooperation to get a grip on the boat crossings across the channel, I will do those things where I believe they can be in the country’s best interests.
Burnham says Russian interference comment did not mean he was questioning legitimacy of Brexit referendum result

Burnham rejected Badenoch’s claim that his comment about Russia on the Rest is Politics podcast meant he did not accept the legitimacy of the Brexit referendum. He said “no such thing”, he told MPs. He went on:

articles.headline: Six Ukrainian energy sites hit by Russia since Trump announced ceasefire, Zelensky says
keyFacts: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia struck six energy facilities hours after US President Donald Trump announced an immediate energy ceasefire.
Ukrainian officials reported blackouts and power cuts in several regions following the overnight strikes, which injured 33 people.
Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov stated that Ukraine does not deserve the respite a ceasefire would bring.
body: - Published
Russia struck six Ukrainian energy facilities hours after US President Donald Trump announced the two countries had agreed to an energy ceasefire, Volodymyr Zelensky has said.
Despite Trump stating on Sunday the truce would be "effective immediately", the Ukrainian president said Russia had hit "our gas stations, energy infrastructure, and other facilities".

There were blackouts in the city of Izyum after a Russian strike destroyed power grids, Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform said, while energy and railway infrastructure in western Ukraine was also targeted overnight.
On Monday, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Ukraine does not deserve the "respite" a ceasefire would bring.
Zelensky said 33 people had been injured in the strikes on energy facilities across the country.
He told Fox News: "We did not attack, while Russia attacked our gas stations, energy infrastructure, and other facilities."
"I think it was Putin's answer to President Trump," he added.
Global conflicts have pushed fuel prices higher ahead of the US midterm elections and on Friday Trump announced a plan to import Russian diesel into the US on Friday.
On Monday, Ukraine's state-owned grid operator Ukrenergo reported "new power cuts" in Kharkiv, Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia due to damage caused to energy equipment by Russian attacks.
Electricity rationing has been introduced in parts of Ukraine to avoid overloading damaged equipment, Ukrenergo said.
Zelensky said on X the strikes were proof Russia was "unwilling to accept an energy ceasefire".
On Monday evening, Kyiv's mayor Vitali Klitschko posted on Telegram that a drone hit a 25-story residential building in the Darnytskyi district.
Several cars in the building's courtyard were also on fire, he said, with one person dead and 11 injured.

When Trump first announced the ceasefire on Sunday, Zelensky said it was "news to him" that a truce was in effect, but he backed the proposed ceasefire as a "major step toward ending the war, if the Americans truly step in now and make sure Russians respect the energy ceasefire".
For months, Ukraine and Russia have been exchanging strikes on energy infrastructure, disrupting energy supplies on both sides.

Moscow has said the installations it hits are legitimate targets as they support Ukraine's military operation, while Zelensky has characterised Ukrainian attacks deep inside Russian territory as part of an effort to "reduce Russia's ability to finance the war".
Analysis by BBC Verify on both Ukrainian and Russian strikes during the war have found both sides have increased their attacks in the lead up to the next winter.
In 2026, BBC Verify has recorded 273 strikes on Russian-controlled oil and gas facilities, more than double the 124 recorded over the same period in 2025.

Separately, analysis of data aggregated by global conflict monitor, the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data project (Acled), recorded 2.4 times as many reported Russian attacks affecting Ukraine's energy network so far this year.
Trump has been urging Ukraine to stop strikes on Russian oil infrastructure, so Russia can fulfil the recently struck deal to release diesel to the US and the global market.
The deal temporarily undoes US sanctions on energy imports, which Zelensky described as a "gift" to Russian President Vladimir Putin.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Britain "strongly supports President Trump's call today for a sustained energy ceasefire to start now", while France, Canada and the EU also expressed support.
However, there has been a mixed response among European officials.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the bloc would welcome an energy ceasefire "when it holds". Kallas said at a meeting of EU foreign ministers on Monday: "We haven't yet seen that also Russia will stick to it."
Meanwhile, Estonia's foreign minister said the ceasefire was "not working".
Additional reporting by Benedict Garman, BBC Verify

articles.headline: WindBorne wins a hefty US Air Force contract for its balloon data
keyFacts: The U.S. Air Force awarded WindBorne Systems a contract worth up to $50 million to buy atmospheric data collected by its autonomous weather balloons.
WindBorne executives stated the non-competitive contract will support the growth of their balloon constellation and fund hardware research and development.
The Air Force pays for data as needed and has ordered $1.7 million worth of regional data so far.
body: The U.S. Air Force will buy data collected by WindBorne Systems‘ fleet of autonomous weather balloons under a new contract that could be worth nearly $50 million to the startup.

WindBorne currently has about 700 weather balloons flying around the globe, collecting atmospheric sensor readings that the company sells to customers and also feeds into its own AI weather forecasting model. WindBorne, founded in 2015 and based in Redwood City, Calif., is one of the first organizations to directly feed empirical data into a deep-learning weather model.

The company has worked closely with the U.S. government, particularly the National Weather Service and the U.S. Air Force and Navy, but this is the single largest contract the company has participated in. The contract is worth up to $49 million, but the Air Force pays only as it needs data. It can place orders for specific regions at specific times. So far, it has ordered $1.7 million worth, and executives expect more orders to follow.

“This is largely a vehicle through which continued growth of the constellation can be supported, as well as some work on research and development to continue to improve the hardware and performance of the balloons,” WindBorne co-founder and CTO Andrey Sushko told TechCrunch. He adds that the contract, which was awarded without competitive bidding, is “a determination by the government that for this capability of collecting global data, we were the only company able to provide it in the way that met their needs for these operations.”

WindBorne CEO John Dean told TechCrunch in August that the company had raised a $37 million Series B round to continue scaling its business. Earlier this summer, the company released the latest version of its forecasting model, WeatherMesh 6, which it says provides more accurate forecasts than the traditional model run by the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), which simulates the atmosphere using the laws of physics.

Since the arrival of transformer model architectures and the ECMWF’s release of a massive weather dataset a few years ago, AI weather forecasting has become one of the more productive uses of deep-learning technology. Meteorologists previously relied on expensive supercomputers running detailed equations that approximate how the atmosphere behaves. Now, end-to-end learning can ingest decades of weather data and issue predictions more quickly.

Models built by frontier labs and government agencies are proving more accurate than traditional forecasts, although it is still a jagged frontier, with both types of forecasts required to enable useful understanding of the weather. Google DeepMind’s latest weather model offers important new capabilities, and its cyclone forecasting tools are becoming increasingly central to how the US government responds to hurricane season.

In August WindBorne became the first organization to send an unpowered flight system — one with no engine — to collect data in the eye of a typhoon. The company maneuvers its balloons by adjusting their altitude, bleeding air, or dropping sand carried as ballast, to send the vehicles into winds that take them where they need to go.

“That’s a pretty novel step, and the two ingredients for that are one, having good wind and weather models, and knowing how to navigate them; and two, having a large enough constellation that you have balloons in the right places,” Sushko said. “It’s one of the first times that a deep-learning model was used for actual operational decisions.”

body: Dragon Quest co-creator Yuji Horii has just released a new game that he says was made (or, rather, prompted) in about half an hour thanks to gen-AI.

In an online post from this weekend, the famed game developer recalled how he created 1983's The Portopia Serial Murder Case mostly on his lonesome. "I came up with the story myself, drew the pictures myself, did the programming myself, and created the game all by myself," Horii wrote on X.

"And now, by using AI, even if I can't draw pictures or program, I can just give instructions to the AI and create a decent game all by myself. It's truly astonishing. By the way, the production time for the game below was just about 30 minutes. Oh, and don't press the boost button," he adds, while linking to a text-based interrogation game.

Horii's love affair with the tech started a while ago. Earlier this year, MMO Dragon Quest 10 teamed up with Google's Gemini AI to power an NPC chatbot called "Chatty Slimey", an in-game character that can talk to players in case they're, you know, starving for human interaction in a massively multiplayer online RPG. The 72-year-old dev defended the decision in an interview with Famitsu, translated by GamesRadar, months later: "Because nowadays AI is really smart, it's fun. It doesn't matter what I ask it, it hardly ever makes things up [anymore]... It's evolving, and lately there are a lot of things you can do with it. Slimey is a conversational partner, so I think it lowers the barrier of entry to interacting with AI."

As noted by VGC, Horii is also toying with the idea of an AI-powered chatbot for one of his future games, as well. He's currently involved with Dragon Quest 12: Beyond Dreams and a surprise sequel to The Portopia Serial Murder Case decades in the making.

Generative-AI and its uses in game development have been hugely controversial in recent years - with players, developers and video game actors worried about job security. Just this month, Google and Unity revealed a quite depressing AI-game-making tool, too.

body: President Donald Trump is re-upping his controversial promise to send a $5,000 dividend check to all U.S. citizens if Republicans maintain control of the House of Representatives and the Senate .

articles.headline: How to get an Emperor Modulator in Arc Raiders
keyFacts: Players can find the Emperor Modulator in the final loot room of the new Emperor dungeon in Arc Raiders.
Obtaining the modulator requires crafting an Emperor Gateway Conduit via the Redirection event and navigating dungeon encounters.
Players need specific equipment like a Snap Hook, Hullcracker, and healing items to survive the dungeon's hazards and enemies.
body: ⚡ Find the Emperor Modulator in the final loot room of the new Emperor dungeon.
⚡ This requires you to craft an Emperor Gateway Conduit via the Redirection event.
⚡ You also have to navigate through the encounters inside The Emperor.
Arc Raiders' Frozen Trail update adds a series of upgrades that let you create "Amplified" weapons, but to do this you'll need a Level 4 Gunsmith bench, which requires an Emperor Modulator to craft.

To get this item, you first have to acquire an Emperor Gateway Conduit blueprint to craft the key required to open The Emperor on the Pendola Pass map. You can apparently find this as a rare drop in Arc Couriers and on other maps, but you can also get it the same way you acquire the materials to craft it:
- Arc Conductive Coupler
- Arc Insulated Coupler
- Arc Plated Coupler

You get all three of these as random drops in the Redirection event on Pendola Pass. Wait for one of the Damaged Emperor Relays on the map to activate, grab the beacon from it, place it down in a quiet open area, and stand back. Harvester payloads will drop in—loot the big central one sticking out the ground for a chance to get one of these materials. You could also try entering The Emperor when someone else unlocks it.
How to complete The Emperor dungeon
Once you have your key to open The Emperor, you're ready to attempt the dungeon by opening the door in the west of Pendola Pass, though you'll need to bring a decent amount of equipment:
- Snap Hook: This is mandatory in my opinion for the platforming puzzles. You could even bring a Grappling Hook as backup in case it breaks, which is a real possibility your first time.
- Anvil or Renegade: You'll need this to destroy the yellow nodes in the more puzzly encounters.
- Hullcracker: This is for destroying the Hydra turrets inside The Emperor. You could also use a Rascal, though it'll slow you down a bit.
- Plenty of healing and shield rechargers: There are many hazards inside the dungeon, so you'll want plenty of healing.
- A Looting augment: You'll want plenty of space to pack in loot, plus a couple of safe pockets for more valuable items, including the modulator.

In terms of a play-by-play of the specific encounters, this walkthrough by crazymrpipz is really good and I can vouch for its accuracy having completed the dungeon myself, though I'll also lay out the encounters below.

The initial section with the corridor, the Hydra turret, and the electrified elevator you make safe by destroying the yellow nodes is always the same, but at the top of the elevator, The Emperor has multiple possible encounter layouts:
The Emperor layout one
1. Pillar Room
You'll slide down a ladder into a room filled with floor-to-ceiling pillars. Destroy the yellow nodes on the pillars to lower a pillar so you can ride it up.
2. Crusher

When the pillar reaches the top, you'll enter a room where the walls close in. Wait for them to pull out, then run to the end without a door, being wary of the gas which lowers stamina. Turn left, wait for the walls to crush in again and quickly platform through the area behind them to reach the door.
3. Hydra Room

You'll approach this room from below in this layout. Being wary of the Hydra turrets around the room, and the crusher below, use your Snap Hook to quickly ascend to the door in the top left side of the room. Destroy any Hydras that activate and target you with your Hullcracker.
The Emperor layout two
1. Container Room
You'll enter a room filled with containers and harvester payload racks. Snap Hook to the top and jump onto the container that lowers to ride it up.
2. Laser Tunnel

This is a tunnel of spinning lasers that deal a lot of damage. If you crouch in the centre, behind the drum that blocks the lasers, you'll be safe. Time your movements to reach the end while taking minimal damage.
3. Hydra Room

In this layout, you approach from above. Drop onto the crate ahead of you, kill the first Hydra that activates, then slide down the rail to your front, run around it, and Snap Hook up to the door on the left before the other two Hydras behind can zero in.
There might be more layouts than this, but the Hydra room seems to be a fixed encounter no matter what. After this point you will:
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
- Descend down a tube, carefully dropping from platform to platform.
- Enter into another room filled with pillars, but this one is a maze.
- Ascend up a couple of tubes by Snap Hook-ing between boxes, avoiding the electrified ones, and climbing ladders to reach a door.

You will enter the final room, drop down onto a lower platform and descend a ladder to the base, though when you touch the floor, the big door at the far end will open and a load of Arc enemies will appear. Hiding is a good idea to see if they leave as opposed to fighting them all. Afterwards, you can loot the containers and also destroy the yellow nodes on either wall to reveal even more loot payloads which pops out of the racks.

One or two of these will contain Emperor Modulators, so make sure to stow one in your safe pocket. After that, you can either leave via the big hatch that opened, or the side doors if you destroyed the yellow nodes.

articles.headline: Lionel Messi names Max Dowman, Arsenal target and Crystal Palace signing among 10 future stars

body: Lionel Messi has updated his list of football’s 10 future stars with Arsenal’s Max Dowman among two Premier League players named.
Shortly after his emotional farewell to international football , the 39-year-old has fittingly picked the youngsters who he believes will shape the game’s next generation.
Messi bid farewell to the international scene shortly after netting his 126th and final goal for Argentina Getty
Messi has previously highlighted the likes of Trent Alexander-Arnold , Phil Foden , Jadon Sancho and Mason Mount as his top wonderkids .
Six years on from his original list, the Inter Miami superstar is now in his third iteration of naming the young stars he is tipping for the top.
Messi’s 10 future stars he believes are football’s ‘next chapter’
Can Uzun
The Eintracht Frankfurt midfielder is one of the more senior names on Messi’s list despite still only being at the tender age of 20.
The German-born 10-cap Turkey international has scored 19 goals and provided 12 assists in 65 Bundesliga matches thus far in his career.
Tomás Aranda
Messi has named just one of his compatriots in his new list, with Boca Juniors talent Aranda earning rave reviews back in Argentina.
The 19-year-old only made his professional debut in January but was handed his senior international debut five months later.
Aranda had registered one assist in six league games for his club since the World Cup before he fractured a fibula in his right leg.
Aranda is one of Argentina’s brightest young talents and is said to be wanted by several Premier League giants Getty
Max Dowman
The future of Arsenal is fresh from receiving three Guinness World Record certificates as a reward for his historic debut season.
The teenager, who made his senior debut in August 2025 , became the Premier League’s youngest ever goalscorer last year en route to helping the Gunners win their first top-flight title for 22 years.
Dowman, who was drafted into first-team training at age 14 , has been tipped by Simon Jordan to become a world-beater like Lamine Yamal .
Dowman became the youngest ever Premier League winner in May Getty
The England Under-19 international, whose heroics last season have seen John Terry and Henry Winter already compare him to Messi and Kaka , has already made an imperious start to the new campaign.
The 16-year-old earned the Carabao Cup Player of the Round award following his two goals against Ipswich last month, which saw him join an exclusive club alongside Wayne Rooney .
Gilberto Mora
The 17-year-old Mexican, one of the breakout stars at Liga MX club Tijuana, has been strongly linked with both Arsenal and Liverpool .
The attacking midfielder underlined his status as his country’s top talent by starting the 3-2 defeat against England at the Azteca in July.
In the round before, Mora became the youngest starter in a World Cup knockout tie after Pele , across the four appearances he made.
Since returning from the tournament, he has scored five goals and registered an assist in seven outings for his boyhood club.
Gilberto Mora made four appearances for Mexico at the World Cup – including against England – and recently scored his first senior international goal Getty
Zavier Gozo
The 19-year-old has been rewarded for making the step up to the Premier League with his first senior appearance for the US national team.
Crystal Palace signed the highly-rated American prospect from Real Salt Lake for a reported £11.1million in August.
Gozo, who made his MLS debut as a 16-year-old in October 2023, scored six goals in RSL’s first 16 league games of the year.
He endured a baptism of fire on his Premier League bow by coming off the bench in the 4-1 defeat to Manchester City , and has also enjoyed a late cameo in the 3-2 loss to Ipswich Town last month.
Gozo made his senior United States debut in the 4-1 win over Peru last month and is trying to break into Crystal Palace’s first team Getty
Jesús Rodríguez
The 20-year-old is hoping to go from strength to strength under Arsenal and Chelsea legend Cesc Fabregas at Como in Italy.
The two-cap Spain international started the club’s first Serie A game of the season but has since had to make do with a substitute role.
Rodriguez is still waiting on his first goal contribution across four outings, and was even sent-off for Spain’s Under-21s last month.
The ex-Real Betis talent, who scored twice and registered nine assists in 31 Serie A games last year, set up Mario Martin’s goal for 12-0 against San Marino before he saw red a few minutes later.
Kees Smit
Earlier this year, Manchester United legend Rio Ferdinand told talkSPORT that he didn’t want his old club to miss out on Smit.
The 20-year-old Netherlands midfielder had previously been named as one of the stars to watch in Europe at the start of last season .
talkSPORT even revealed that Newcastle and Crystal Palace were competing with Real Madrid to sign the AZ Alkmaar star.
However, no summer move to the Premier League transpired , and Smit has registered two assists in five Eredivisie matches this term.
Smit was a surprise omission from the Netherlands’ World Cup squad after his impressive season Getty
Chloe Sarwie
Messi also named three future stars of women’s football in his list, with Chelsea’s Sarwie the headline selection for England fans.
The 17-year-old made seven senior appearances for Chelsea last season and was in the Lionesses squad for the Under-20 World Cup.
Giovanna Waksman
The Brazilian youth international only joined OL Lyonnes in March, having first come through the ranks at Botafogo in her homeland.
The 17-year-old is still waiting for her first senior appearance at club level this season but is in double digits for goals for Brazil’s U17s.
Lotta Wrede
The 18-year-old has made three appearances in the Frauen-Bundesliga this season with her childhood Hamburg outfit.
The club’s No.32 has also scored three times in nine appearances for Germany ‘s Under-19s and has been linked with a move to Barcelona .
